intended_object: The "lower cut" operation on admissible layers. Given a subobject D ≤ B with B/D in P, it sends a nested pair L ≤ U of subobjects of B, with U/L in P, to the pair (L ∩ D, U), whose lower end lies in D. It is the left adjoint (reflector) to the inclusion of layers with lower end ≤ D. This is inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the Galois-connection theorem that follows it.
explanation:
The map sends the layer (L, U) to the layer (L ⊓ D, U), and the subtype proof records L ⊓ D ≤ D. This is exactly what the docstring describes.

The new layer is admissible for the reason the docstring gives. The map U/(L∩D) → U/L × B/D is a monomorphism. U/L is in P by hypothesis and B/D is in P by `hD`. Because P is closed under binary products and under subobjects, U/(L∩D) is in P. So the hypotheses on P and on D are exactly the ones the construction needs.

The later theorem `lowerCut_galoisConnection` checks that this map is left adjoint to `lowerInclusion` in the layer order (lower end ordered in reverse, upper end ordered normally). This confirms that it is the intended reflector.

An abelian category is the natural setting, since cokernels and intersections of subobjects are used. Mathlib has no general counterpart, because the structure is specific to this library.
